source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Quincy is Washington's largest publicly specified data center by IT capacity, at 36 MW, and accounts for 60 percent of the state's declared data center load.

The 36 MW IT load sits inside 720,000 square feet of technical space, about 50 watts per square foot, a density consistent with high-density compute facilities. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, that capacity would support roughly 900 racks, but the operator publishes no tenant mix or workload type, so the campus cannot be confirmed as AI infrastructure from these facts alone.

Washington has 46 mapped data center facilities, yet only two disclose capacity figures on operator specification pages. That makes this campus a rare public anchor for the state's grid load, while the true share of Washington's data center power demand remains unknown. No power certifications, utility partnership details, or announced expansion are published, and the site's suitability score of 68 reflects that missing expansion signal. Whether the 36 MW represents current utilization or available headroom, and whether the grid connection can support growth, is not stated.
